business: Trans American Trucking & Warehouse (Trans American Trucking Service, Inc.)
summary: Family-owned, asset-based heavy-haul and flatbed carrier founded in 1976, headquartered at 602 New Market Ave in South Plainfield with terminals/warehouses in Baltimore MD and South Hampton NH, roughly 90 employees, 57 power units and 200+ specialized trailers, plus 300,000+ sq ft of warehouse and customs-bonded storage. Freight intake runs through a web quote-request form, a rates@transamer.com inbox and phone numbers for each terminal's dispatch/warehouse rather than any online booking or portal, and all permitting, escort and dispatch coordination is done in-house. Growth is steady (50th-anniversary press release in May 2026, a 2024 South Plainfield warehouse addition, and a $33.25M sale of a surplus 8.8-acre outdoor-storage lot in 2025), while public feedback is almost entirely employee-side and mixed.

facts.fact: Founded in 1976 in Edison, NJ by Ron McGraw and Jim Skow as a flatbed and van carrier; headquarters has been in South Plainfield since 1986 and the company marked its 50-plus anniversary in March 2026.
Employs about 90 people from the tristate area as drivers, dispatchers, warehouse personnel, office staff, and in accounting, IT, permitting and heavy-haul departments, plus a safety director.

Fleet is 50+ late-model power units and 200+ specialized trailers, with terminals and warehouse locations in South Plainfield NJ, Baltimore MD and South Hampton NH; drivers average 20+ years of experience and the company cites 90% workforce retention.

FMCSA SAFER snapshot (data as of 11/09/2026): USDOT 229132, ACTIVE, 57 power units, 44 drivers, MCS-150 mileage 2,469,448 for 2024, satisfactory safety rating; 293 driver and 264 vehicle inspections in the prior 24 months with 3 reported crashes.

Warehouse footprint: 300,000 sq ft main warehouse plus a 40,000 sq ft auxiliary warehouse for containerization, drayage and storage (press release); the site advertises 350,000 sq ft indoor plus 200,000 sq ft secure outdoor storage across facilities.

Growth/sale: Trans American Trucking Services sold its 8.84-acre industrial outdoor storage site at 115 St. Nicholas Ave in South Plainfield for $33.25 million in January 2025 (buyers Oliver Street Capital and Bain Capital Real Estate, brokered by NAI James E. Hanson).

Locations page lists per-site dispatch and warehouse phone numbers: HQ 602 New Market Ave (toll-free 800-526-7596, dispatch 908-755-9000, warehouse 732-424-2300), 110 Snyder Road warehouse 908-754-8600, Baltimore MD dispatch 410-282-2050, South Hampton NH dispatch 603-580-4379.

Site structured data lists opening hours Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00 and a single published quote intake path (quote-request page, rates@transamer.com, 800-526-7596); the FAQ states permitting is handled by an in-house permits department with company route surveys and that HAZMAT classes 3, 4, 8 and 9 are authorized.

operations_signals: Quote intake is a manual hand-off: the quote-request page asks shippers to submit a form and says a rate specialist 'will be in contact with you shortly' — no instant rate, no online booking, no customer portal (https://www.transamer.com/quote-request).

Every terminal is reached by its own phone line and fax (NJ/MD/NH dispatch and warehouse numbers, with fax numbers published in site structured data), which suggests phone/fax/email coordination between sites (https://www.transamer.com/posts/locations).
Stated business hours are Monday-Friday 08:00-17:00 with no published after-hours or weekend coverage, despite 24/7 facility video surveillance (https://www.transamer.com/our-history).

Heavy-haul moves require in-house permitting, route surveys, police escorts and road closures, and the site says permits, escorts and dispatch work together on each move — a document- and coordination-heavy workflow (https://www.transamer.com/heavy-haul).

Warehouse services include container stripping/stuffing, transloading, customs-bonded storage, export packing and off-site packing at customer or port locations, i.e. per-job scheduling across multiple yards (https://www.transamer.com/logistics).
Service area is the contiguous US plus Canada, with NJ, MD and NH facilities positioned near the Port of NY/NJ, Port of Baltimore and I-95 (https://www.transamer.com/posts/locations).
hiring_signals: Open dispatcher role at the South Hampton, NH terminal (posted via recruiting firm KJ Media): coordinating freight from the base location and securing return loads to maintain equipment utilization (https://recruiterflow.com/db_894374fea70880fe97c206119efbdb91/jobs/2086).

Dispatcher posting for the South Plainfield, NJ office listed on SimplyHired with a short, general description — 'manage daily trucks', 'computer knowledge / Excel a plus', willing to train (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/Wb4ULSU_boX0Cu_AHME1J0hfhWXc3jn1-v6UTdlLeIPwb6IjooBESA).

Over-the-road driver opening at the NH terminal requiring coordination with dispatchers and customers plus paper/electronic logs and pre/post-trip documentation (https://www.classadrivers.com/truck-driving-jobs/detail/2626257/over-the-road-driver).

The corporate site has no careers page (https://www.transamer.com/careers and /services both return 404); driver recruiting runs through a separate site (transamericantruckingjobs.com) and third-party boards, and a Class A Drivers company profile for them is marked inactive (https://static.classadrivers.com/trucking-companies/profile/5747/trans-american-trucking-service-inc).

Job-board snippets show an employer-provided salary of about $50K for the South Plainfield dispatcher role and a broad benefits package (401k, medical/dental/vision, PTO) in driver ads (https://www.glassdoor.com/job-listing/warehouse-dispatcher-zimmer-biomet-JV_IC1126720_KO0,20_KE21,34.htm?jl=1010161514181).
review_themes: Customer-side reviews are effectively absent: the trucking/warehouse Yelp listing has no substantive review content surfaced, and no BBB profile for this company was found, so no shipper complaints or praise could be verified (https://www.yelp.com/biz/trans-american-trucking-south-plainfield-2).

Employee reviews are mixed: Glassdoor shows 2.7/5 with 46% would recommend to a friend across 7 reviews, and 13% positive business outlook (https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Trans-American-Trucking-Service-Reviews-E1090845.htm).

Indeed shows a 3.7/5 company rating for the South Plainfield location, with reviews praising pay, benefits and the fleet/equipment while criticizing shop management (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Trans-American-Trucking-Service).

Recurring employee criticism centers on management and structure ('no real structure to the shop', favoritism) and expensive benefits, alongside praise for long tenure and equipment quality (https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Trans-American-Trucking-Service-South-Plainfield-NJ-Reviews-EI_IE1090845.0,31_IL.32,51_IC1126995.htm).
tech_footprint: Marketing site is a small brochure build (Tailwind-based, ~6 pages: home, trucking service, warehouse, import/export, history, locations) with a quote-request form and an FAQ page; no login, tracking portal or shipper self-service (https://www.transamer.com/).
Analytics: Fathom Analytics script embedded site-wide (privacy-first, cookieless) — minimal marketing measurement stack (https://www.transamer.com/our-history).

Rich schema.org markup on the site (Corporation/LocalBusiness, OfferCatalog, FAQPage with a named Director of International Projects as answer author) plus a published Rules Tariff PDF — content is structured but not interactive (https://www.transamer.com/our-history).

Claims 'smart fleet technology' connecting trucks to the back office with real-time asset visibility and telematics, but names no vendor; no customer-facing tracking is advertised (https://www.transamer.com/).
Social presence limited to LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram; no blog, news feed or gated content on the corporate site (https://www.transamer.com/our-history).

Third-party listings are inconsistent — Yelp still shows a St. Nicholas Ave address for the company, which was the outdoor-storage lot sold in 2025 — suggesting unmanaged directory data (https://www.yelp.com/biz/trans-american-trucking-south-plainfield-2).
growth_signals: 50th-anniversary press release (May 2026) states the company has run about two million miles annually for the past two years and that leadership intends to expand and win new business (https://www.einpresswire.com/article/910189908/trans-american-trucking-warehouse-celebrates-50-years).

Company LinkedIn post (2024) announcing a new warehouse in South Plainfield, consistent with a warehouse footprint that grew to 300,000+ sq ft plus a 40,000 sq ft auxiliary building (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/trans-american-trucking-service-inc_check-out-our-new-warehouse-in-south-plainfield-activity-7175605753448169473-itu-).

Sold a non-core 8.84-acre industrial outdoor storage lot at 115 St. Nicholas Ave for $33.25M in January 2025 — capital recycling rather than contraction of the operating footprint (https://re-nj.com/investors-buy-south-plainfield-industrial-outdoor-storage-site-for-33-million-nai-hanson-says).

Leadership transition: co-founder Jim Skow retired in 2014; Jeff McGraw (45+ years experience) is vice president, Craig McGraw is national VP of sales and marketing, and second/third-generation family members hold comptroller and operational roles (https://www.einpresswire.com/article/910189908/trans-american-trucking-warehouse-celebrates-50-years).
Memberships and certifications (C-TPAT, FAST, TWIC, RICA, SC&RA, NJMTA, CVSA) position it for port drayage and project cargo work in the Northeast (https://www.transamer.com/contact-us).
decision_maker: Craig McGraw, National VP of Sales and Marketing (named in the company's own 50th-anniversary press release, https://www.einpresswire.com/article/910189908/trans-american-trucking-warehouse-celebrates-50-years); Jeff McGraw, Vice President, is the other named senior leader. Founder Ron McGraw is listed as the company's principal on Glassdoor but not on the company's own site.

inferences.inference: Quote turnaround is likely measured in hours-to-days and depends on a person, which is the highest-value place for an AI agent.
inferences.reasoning: The only published intake is a form/email that routes to 'rate specialists' who contact the shipper later; no instant quoting, rate API or booking engine is visible anywhere on the site.

inferences.inference: Multi-site dispatch across NJ, MD and NH is coordinated by phone/fax/email with no shared customer-facing system, creating hand-off and double-entry risk.
inferences.reasoning: Each terminal publishes separate dispatch and warehouse phone and fax numbers, and the site advertises no portal, TMS brand or tracking product that would span sites.

inferences.inference: Permitting and escort coordination is a document-heavy bottleneck that scales headcount with volume.
inferences.reasoning: The site says permits are procured in-house with company route surveys and that permits staff, escort drivers, drivers and dispatch must all coordinate per move; 300,000 lb superloads move through congested Northeast states with per-state permits.

inferences.inference: Recruiting and applicant intake is weak/near-invisible, which likely slows backfilling dispatch and driver seats.
inferences.reasoning: No careers page on the corporate site (both /careers and /services 404), recruiting is outsourced to a marketing vendor (KJ Media) and boards, and a third-party driver profile for the company is flagged inactive.

inferences.inference: Employee-side sentiment (2.7 Glassdoor, management complaints) points to process and communication gaps rather than pay, which is where agent-assisted internal workflows (status updates, SOP lookups, exception alerts) may earn goodwill.
inferences.reasoning: Reviews consistently praise pay/benefits and equipment but criticize structure and management; no customer reviews exist to test service quality directly.

inferences.inference: Zero customer reviews is more likely a B2B/contract-freight characteristic than a service problem.
inferences.reasoning: Revenue appears to come from manufacturers, utilities and project-cargo shippers contracted through sales staff rather than consumer bookings, so review volume is naturally near zero.

data_gaps: No customer/shipper reviews could be verified: Yelp blocked automated access (HTTP 403), no BBB profile was found, and Google Business Profile review text is not accessible without a JS browser/login.
Indeed, Glassdoor, LinkedIn and CarrierSource pages returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches; their ratings and review themes above come from search-result snippets only.
No revenue figure, fleet valuation or customer list published; size is estimated from the press release (90 employees) and FMCSA (57 power units, 44 drivers).
Current job count and full job descriptions could not be confirmed — SimplyHired/ZipRecruiter/RecruiterFlow postings are JS-rendered or blocked, so only snippets were usable.
No customer-facing TMS, EDI or booking vendor is named, so the internal dispatch stack (e.g., McLeod, TMW, Turvo) is unknown.
Whether an after-hours or 24/7 dispatch line exists is unknown; only Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00 hours are published.
Contact and quote forms were not submitted per task limits, so actual form routing and response time were not tested.
